⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. OpenDefence on Kubernetes (opendefence-platform) is in closed alpha and under rapid, breaking development. This page describes a moving target and will most likely be superseded by the documentation that ships with the first public release — treat everything here as provisional, and do not rely on it for a production deployment.

This page maps the Matrix product as it is deployed by pvarki/opendefence-platform — the most complex product in the stack: Synapse, the Matrix Authentication Service (MAS), LiveKit and the Element Call JWT service behind four hostnames, with authentication federated into the platform's Keycloak. It is for developers and operators who need to know what runs where; for building your own integration against the same pattern, see the worked example instead.

Component inventory

The product lives in namespace app-matrix; apart from its two Postgres clusters, everything runs in a single Deployment matrix (strategy Recreate, one pod, Linkerd-injected) with six containers:

Container Image Port Role
matrixrmapi ghcr.io/pvarki/matrix-integration:1.3.0-260714 8012 Integration API — the rmapi product contract
synapse-server ghcr.io/pvarki/synapse-server:1.2.0-260708 8008 Matrix homeserver; federation disabled via SYNAPSE_FEDERATION=off
mas ghcr.io/pvarki/mas-server:1.0.0-260708 8082 web, 8081 internal (Service mas:8080) Matrix Authentication Service — OIDC front for Synapse
livekit livekit/livekit-server:v1.13.3 7880 signalling + raw media ports SFU for Element Call
matrix-rtc ghcr.io/element-hq/lk-jwt-service:0.5.0 6080 Issues LiveKit JWTs to authenticated Matrix users
matrix-ui-nginx nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:alpine 8080 Serves integration UI files and /.well-known/matrix/*

Three containers boot through entry scripts mounted from ConfigMaps (k8s/app-matrix/base/init-scripts/): mas-entrypoint.sh (OIDC bootstrap + key generation, see below), synapse-entrypoint.sh (renders homeserver.yaml from a template, expands the federation policy, waits for Postgres) and livekit-entrypoint.sh (resolves the node IP at runtime, see the media plane section).

State is split across two CNPG clusters — matrix-postgres (5Gi, Synapse) and mas-postgres (1Gi, MAS), both postgresql:18.0-system-trixie, both instances: 1 — and three PVCs: synapse-server-data (5Gi — media store and the rendered homeserver.yaml), mas-data (1Gi — MAS signing keys and the persisted OIDC client registration) and matrix-data (1Gi — integration data). As everywhere on the platform, no backups are configured and every database is a single instance. All secrets (Synapse macaroon key, MAS↔Synapse shared secret, MAS admin client secret, MAS encryption secret, LiveKit API secret) are generated in-cluster by the matrix-secrets ExternalSecret — see Data & secrets.

The whole shape — one pod, its Services, four hostnames plus the root-domain discovery route, and the raw media Service that bypasses Traefik:

blocks.html:
Hostnames & discovery

The product spans four dedicated hostnames plus a carve-out on the root domain and a UI path on the shared mtls.<domain> host (<domain> = OPENDEFENCE_HOST, locally localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi); IngressRoutes live in k8s/app-matrix/overlays/{local,cloud}/matrix.ingressroute.yaml:

Host / path Backend mTLS
<domain> /.well-known/matrix/* matrix:8080 (nginx) none
synapse.<domain> synapse-server:8008 none
synapse.<domain> /_matrix/client/*/(login|logout|refresh) mas:8080 none
synapse.<domain> /_synapse/admin synapse-server:8008, IP-allowlisted none
mas.<domain> mas:8080 none
matrix.<domain> /api matrix:8012 (matrixrmapi) mtls-strict + callsign chain
matrix-rtc.<domain> /livekit/jwt, /livekit/sfu matrix-rtc:6080 / matrix-rtc:7880 none
mtls.<domain> /ui/matrix matrix:8080 (nginx) mtls-optional

Why discovery lives on the root domain while the homeserver lives on **synapse.<domain>**: Matrix identifies a server by the domain in its user IDs. Here server_name is the root <domain>, so users are @callsign:<domain> — but the actual homeserver answers on synapse.<domain>. The Matrix spec bridges that gap with well-known delegation: clients and servers resolving <domain> fetch https://<domain>/.well-known/matrix/server ({"m.server":"synapse.<domain>:443"}) and /.well-known/matrix/client (base_url → https://synapse.<domain>, plus the MSC4143 rtc_foci entry pointing Element Call at the LiveKit JWT service). Those two JSON files are overlay-templated (wellknown-server.json / wellknown-client.json), mounted into matrix-ui-nginx, and exposed by the matrix-wellknown IngressRoute — a PathPrefix(/.well-known/matrix) carve-out on the same root host that otherwise serves the Deploy App UI.

Two details on the synapse.<domain> route are easy to miss. First, /_synapse/admin is wrapped in the app-local synapse-admin-deny middleware — an ipAllowList of 127.0.0.1/32, which no request arriving through the edge can match, so the admin API is effectively cluster-internal only (admin-token auth still applies on top). Second, legacy Matrix clients that POST to /_matrix/client/*/login|logout|refresh are routed to MAS, not Synapse — MAS implements the compatibility layer for pre-OIDC clients.

Authentication chain

Synapse holds no credentials: password_config.enabled: false, enable_registration: false. Instead homeserver.yaml sets matrix_authentication_service.enabled: true, delegating all auth to MAS over a pod-local endpoint (MAS_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8082) secured by the generated MAS_SYNAPSE_SECRET.

MAS in turn federates upstream to the platform's Keycloak: KC_ISSUER=https://kc.<domain>:9443/realms/RASENMAEHER — the same realm rmapi provisions users into, backed by OpenLDAP (see Core services). So a Matrix login is ultimately a Keycloak login with the user's Deploy App identity. A full login from an Element client:

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as ElementClient
    participant N as WellKnown
    participant S as Synapse
    participant M as MAS
    participant K as Keycloak
    C->>N: GET /.well-known/matrix/client at the root domain
    N-->>C: m.homeserver base_url = the synapse subdomain
    C->>S: discover auth capabilities
    S-->>C: auth delegated to MAS
    C->>M: OIDC authorization request
    M-->>C: redirect to Keycloak realm RASENMAEHER (port 9443)
    C->>K: sign in (LDAP-backed credential check)
    K-->>M: authorization code, token exchange
    M-->>C: Matrix access + refresh tokens
    C->>S: client API calls with MAS-issued token
    S->>M: introspect token (shared secret)
    S-->>C: Matrix session established

blocks.html: The MAS↔Keycloak client is not pre-provisioned — mas-entrypoint.sh registers it on first boot. If /data/oidc/registration.json is missing, the script calls /kc_client_init get_jwt and register_oidc using /pvarki/kraftwerk-init.json (Keycloak endpoint from its kc block; registered client name MAS from oidc.client_registration), then persists the returned client_id/client_secret on the mas-data PVC — making the bootstrap idempotent across restarts. The same script generates RSA and EC P-256 signing keys on first boot, renders config.yaml from a template with envsubst, runs mas-cli config check, and only then starts the server. The MAS admin client is 000000000000000RASENMAEHER.

blocks.html:
Element Call media plane

Element Call needs two things: a LiveKit JWT proving who you are, and a media path to the SFU. The JWT comes from lk-jwt-service (the matrix-rtc container) at https://matrix-rtc.<domain>/livekit/jwt — it confirms the caller's Matrix identity with the homeserver (LIVEKIT_FULL_ACCESS_HOMESERVERS=<domain>) and signs a LiveKit token with the shared LIVEKIT_API_SECRET (key name opendefence). Signalling then runs over wss://matrix-rtc.<domain>/livekit/sfu through Traefik to LiveKit's :7880 (both paths share the matrix-rtc-stripprefix middleware).

Media itself never touches Traefik. The matrix-rtc-media Service exposes the raw ports directly: 7881 ICE/TCP, 7882 media/UDP, 3478 TURN/UDP, 5349 TURN/TLS. Locally that is a NodePort Service bound through kind's extraPortMappings; in cloud it is a LoadBalancer with allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false and externalTrafficPolicy: Local — the latter so LiveKit sees the real client source IP, which ICE/TURN needs. The pod's Linkerd annotation config.linkerd.io/skip-inbound-ports: 3478,5349,7881,7882 keeps the mesh proxy off the media path too.

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as ElementCall
    participant T as Traefik
    participant J as LkJwtService
    participant S as Synapse
    participant L as LiveKit
    C->>T: POST /livekit/jwt on the matrix-rtc host
    T->>J: stripPrefix, forward to port 6080
    J->>S: verify caller's Matrix OpenID token
    S-->>J: identity confirmed
    J-->>C: LiveKit JWT
    C->>T: wss /livekit/sfu on the matrix-rtc host
    T->>L: signalling to port 7880
    Note over C,L: media bypasses Traefik entirely
    C->>L: media 7882/udp or TURN 3478/udp, 5349/tls
    L-->>C: via Service matrix-rtc-media

blocks.html:
One LiveKit quirk drives livekit-entrypoint.sh: LiveKit requires a literal node IP in its config. The script reads turn.domain from /etc/livekit.yaml (locally matrix-rtc.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi), resolves it with getent at container start, substitutes it for the __NODE_IP__ placeholder and then execs livekit-server. TURN/TLS on 5349 uses the matrix-rtc-tls certificate mounted at /certs.

Platform integration

matrixrmapi is the product's face toward the platform hub, following the standard integration pattern: rmapi reaches it in-cluster at http://matrix.app-matrix.svc.cluster.local:8012/ (from the core's kraftwerk-rasenmaeher-init registry), and the matrix pod mounts its own kraftwerk-init.json pointing back at http://rmapi.opendefence-system.svc.cluster.local:8000/ with certcn pinned to rmapi.opendefence-system.serviceaccount.identity.linkerd.cluster.local (MTLS_TRUST_L5D=true) — in-cluster calls are plain HTTP wrapped in Linkerd mTLS, and the integration only trusts the pinned rmapi identity.

The integration also shapes the Matrix side of onboarding: homeserver.yaml sets auto_join_rooms to #<deployment>-space, #<deployment>-general, #<deployment>-helpdesk and #<deployment>-offtopic (all :<domain>), with autocreate_auto_join_rooms: false — room creation is deliberately not left to Synapse — and auto_join_mxid_localpart: matrixrmapi-bot. UI files written by matrixrmapi into a shared emptyDir are served by matrix-ui-nginx at mtls.<domain>/ui/matrix. How the integration API itself works (endpoints, user lifecycle, the bot) is covered by the worked example: Matrix — not repeated here.

Experimental notes

Several pieces of this stack sit ahead of the Matrix spec — expect them to change or break across Synapse/Element upgrades:

  • experimental_features in homeserver.yaml enables msc3266_enabled (room summaries) and msc4222_enabled (sync v2 state_after) — both pre-standard MSCs.
  • Element Call discovery relies on MSC4143 RTC foci: the org.matrix.msc4143.rtc_foci key (type livekit, pointing at LIVEKIT_JWT_URL) is injected both into /.well-known/matrix/client and via Synapse's extra_well_known_client_content. This is a proposal, not accepted spec.
  • Federation is off (federation_domain_whitelist: []) and trusted_key_servers: [] — the deployment is deliberately an island; matrix.org is never consulted as a key server.
